claim: Cyclic diguanylate monophosphate (c-di-GMP) drives the transition between planktonic and biofilm growth in many bacterial species.
source: The second messenger signaling molecule cyclic diguanylate monophosphate (c-di-GMP) drives the transition between planktonic and biofilm growth in many bacterial species.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about c-di-GMP function in bacteria.

claim: Pseudomonas aeruginosa has two surface sensing systems that produce c-di-GMP in response to surface adherence.
source: Pseudomonas aeruginosa has two surface sensing systems that produce c-di-GMP in response to surface adherence.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work on the Wsp and Pil-Chp systems described later in the manuscript.

claim: The Wsp system generates heterogeneity in surface sensing, resulting in two physiologically distinct subpopulations of cells.
source: Here, we describe how the Wsp system generates heterogeneity in surface sensing, resulting in two physiologically distinct subpopulations of cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: One subpopulation has elevated c-di-GMP and produces biofilm matrix, serving as the founders of initial microcolonies.
source: One subpopulation has elevated c-di-GMP and produces biofilm matrix, serving as the founders of initial microcolonies.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing correlation between high c-di-GMP reporter activity and polysaccharide production.

claim: The other subpopulation has low c-di-GMP and engages in surface motility, allowing for exploration of the surface.
source: The other subpopulation has low c-di-GMP and engages in surface motility, allowing for exploration of the surface.
evidence: This is supported by tracking data showing inverse correlation between c-di-GMP levels and surface motility.

claim: Heterogeneity in c-di-GMP strongly correlates to surface behavior for descendent cells.
source: We also show that this heterogeneity strongly correlates to surface behavior for descendent cells.
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracking experiments showing multi-generational correlations.

claim: After surface attachment, P. aeruginosa engages in a division of labor that persists across generations, accelerating early biofilm formation and surface exploration.
source: Together, our results suggest that after surface attachment, P. aeruginosa engages in a division of labor that persists across generations, accelerating early biofilm formation and surface exploration.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings supported by data and inference.

claim: Biofilms are dense aggregates of cells producing extracellular matrix components that hold the community together.
source: Biofilms are dense aggregates of cells producing extracellular matrix components that hold the community together.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about biofilm structure.

claim: The biofilm mode of growth allows cells to maintain close proximity to nutrients, promotes exchange of genetic material, and confers cells protection from a variety of chemical and environmental stresses.
source: The biofilm mode of growth is beneficial for bacteria in that it allows cells to maintain close proximity to nutrients, promotes exchange of genetic material, and confers cells protection from a variety of chemical and environmental stresses (e.g. nutrient limitation, desiccation, and shear forces), as well as engulfment by protozoa in the environment or by phagocytes in a host (Davey and O'toole, 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: In many bacterial species, including P. aeruginosa, elevated c-di-GMP results in repression of flagellar motility genes, while promoting expression of genes involved in producing a biofilm matrix.
source: In many bacterial species, including P. aeruginosa, elevated c-di-GMP results in repression of flagellar motility genes, while promoting expression of genes involved in producing a biofilm matrix (Römling et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The P. aeruginosa biofilm matrix is composed of a combination of polysaccharides (including Pel and Psl), proteins (including the adhesin CdrA), and extracellular DNA.
source: The P. aeruginosa biofilm matrix is composed of a combination of polysaccharides (including Pel and Psl), proteins (including the adhesin CdrA), and extracellular DNA (Ma et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The cdrA, pel and psl genes are all transcriptionally induced under conditions of high c-di-GMP.
source: The cdrA, pel and psl genes are all transcriptionally induced under conditions of high c-di-GMP (Starkey et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: P. aeruginosa has at least two distinct surface sensing systems, the Wsp and the Pil-Chp systems, that when activated, lead to biofilm formation.
source: P. aeruginosa has at least two distinct surface sensing systems, the Wsp and the Pil-Chp systems, that when activated, lead to biofilm formation.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: The Wsp system senses an unknown surface-related signal through WspA, a membrane-bound protein homologous to methyl-accepting chemotaxis proteins (MCPs).
source: The Wsp system senses an unknown surface-related signal (recently proposed to be membrane perturbation [Chen et al., 2014]) through WspA, a membrane-bound protein homologous to methyl-accepting chemotaxis proteins (MCPs).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Activation of the Wsp system stimulates phosphorylation of the diguanylate cyclase WspR, which leads to the formation of aggregates of phosphorylated WspR (WspR-P) in the form of visible subcellular clusters.
source: Activation of this system stimulates phosphorylation of the diguanylate cyclase WspR, which leads to the formation of aggregates of phosphorylated WspR (WspR-P) in the form of visible subcellular clusters.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Aggregation of WspR-P potentiates its activity, increasing c-di-GMP synthesis.
source: This aggregation of WspR-P potentiates its activity, increasing c-di-GMP synthesis (Huangyutitham et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The Pil-Chp chemosensory-like system initiates a hierarchical cascade of second messenger signaling in response to a surface.
source: In comparison, the Pil-Chp chemosensory-like system initiates a hierarchical cascade of second messenger signaling in response to a surface (Luo et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: An increase in cellular cAMP levels occurs through activation of the adenylate cyclase CyaB by the Pil-Chp complex.
source: First, an increase in cellular cAMP levels occurs through activation of the adenylate cyclase CyaB by the Pil-Chp complex.
evidence: This statement describes the mechanism of the Pil-Chp system based on prior work.

claim: Increased cAMP increases expression of genes involved in type IV pilus biogenesis, including PilY1.
source: This increases expression of genes involved in type IV pilus biogenesis, including PilY1.
evidence: This statement describes the mechanism of the Pil-Chp system based on prior work.

claim: PilY1 is associated with the type IV pilus and harbors a Von Willebrand motif, which is involved in mechanosensing in eukaryotic systems.
source: PilY1 is associated with the type IV pilus and harbors a Von Willebrand motif, which is involved in mechanosensing in eukaryotic systems (Kuchma et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: PilY1 may be involved in the mechanosensing of surfaces.
source: Thus, it has been proposed that this protein may be involved in the mechanosensing of surfaces (Persat et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on prior work, indicated by 'has been proposed'.

claim: The output of the Pil-Chp system is through the diguanylate cyclase, SadC, resulting in an increase in cellular c-di-GMP levels.
source: The output of this second signal is through the diguanylate cyclase, SadC, resulting in an increase in cellular c-di-GMP levels.
evidence: This statement describes the mechanism of the Pil-Chp system based on prior work.

claim: PilY1 is required to be associated with polarly-localized type IV pili in order to stimulate c-di-GMP production.
source: Unlike the Wsp system, which localizes laterally along the cell (O'Connor et al., 2012), PilY1 is required to be associated with polarly-localized type IV pili in order to stimulate c-di-GMP production (Luo et al., 2015; Kuchma et al., 2010), suggesting that P. aeruginosa deploys both polar and laterally localized systems to promote c-di-GMP synthesis in response to a surface.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: P. aeruginosa deploys both polar and laterally localized systems to promote c-di-GMP synthesis in response to a surface.
source: Unlike the Wsp system, which localizes laterally along the cell (O'Connor et al., 2012), PilY1 is required to be associated with polarly-localized type IV pili in order to stimulate c-di-GMP production (Luo et al., 2015; Kuchma et al., 2010), suggesting that P. aeruginosa deploys both polar and laterally localized systems to promote c-di-GMP synthesis in response to a surface.
evidence: This is an inference based on the localization patterns of the two systems.

claim: Bacteria in biofilms exhibit phenotypic heterogeneity due to chemical variation within the biofilm itself, including gradients of oxygen, nutrients, and pH.
source: Bacteria in biofilms have long been appreciated to exhibit phenotypic heterogeneity due to chemical variation within the biofilm itself, including gradients of oxygen (Wessel et al., 2014), nutrients (Schreiber et al., 2016), and pH (Vroom et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Environmental conditions are sensed by individual bacterial cells, leading to differential gene expression and metabolic activities even within a genetically homogeneous population.
source: These environmental conditions are sensed by individual bacterial cells, leading to differential gene expression and metabolic activities even within a genetically homogeneous population (Stewart and Franklin, 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Division of labor refers to cases where genetic or phenotypic heterogeneity results in subpopulations of cells cooperating to perform distinct tasks that provide an overall fitness benefit to the population.
source: Specifically, the term 'division of labor' refers to cases where genetic or phenotypic heterogeneity results in subpopulations of cells cooperating to perform distinct tasks that provide an overall fitness benefit to the population (West and Cooper, 2016).
evidence: This is a definition supported by a citation.

claim: Genetic and phenotypic variation in surface motility and polysaccharide production among individual bacterial cells within a biofilm can represent a division of labor that is required to achieve the architecture and structural integrity of the biofilm matrix.
source: In particular, there is a rich body of literature demonstrating that genetic (Kim et al., 2016; Dragoš et al., 2018; Klausen et al., 2003) and phenotypic variation (Klauck et al., 2018; Serra et al., 2015; Haagensen et al., 2007) in surface motility and polysaccharide production among individual bacterial cells within a biofilm can represent a division of labor that is required to achieve the architecture and structural integrity of the biofilm matrix (van Gestel et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: c-di-GMP signaling can drive phenotypic heterogeneity among populations of single cells exposed to the same environmental inputs.
source: Beyond heterogeneity as a result of variation in environmental signals, recent single-cell analyses have revealed that c-di-GMP signaling can drive phenotypic heterogeneity among populations of single cells exposed to the same environmental inputs.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work described in the following sentences.

claim: Planktonic P. aeruginosa achieve heterogeneity among very low levels of c-di-GMP through asymmetrical partitioning of a diguanylate cyclase during cell division, leading to diverse swimming motility behaviors.
source: Planktonic P. aeruginosa have been shown to achieve heterogeneity among very low levels of c-di-GMP through assymetrical partitioning of a diguanylate cyclase during cell division, leading to diverse swimming molitity behaviors (Kulasekara et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Asymmetrical cell division mechanism generates two populations of P. aeruginosa, one piliated and one flagellated, that are each required for efficient tissue colonization.
source: More recently, this same assymetrical cell division mechanism was shown to generate two populations of P. aeruginosa, one piliated and one flagellated, that are each required for efficient tissue colonization (Laventie et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: PAO1 cellular c-di-GMP levels are 4.4-fold higher after 4 hr of growth attached to a surface compared to planktonic growth.
source: As expected, we observed that PAO1 cellular c-di-GMP levels are 4.4-fold higher (±0.78 SD, N = 3, p≤0.05) after 4 hr of growth attached to a surface compared to planktonic growth (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: After just 30 min of surface attachment, pelA transcript levels had increased almost 10-fold compared to planktonically grown cells.
source: We found that after just 30 min of surface attachment, pelA transcript levels had increased almost 10-fold compared to planktonically grown cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Transcription of the pel operon is directly and positively controlled by high cellular levels of c-di-GMP.
source: This is consistent with previously published literature showing that transcription of the pel operon is directly and positively controlled by high cellular levels of c-di-GMP (Hickman and Harwood, 2008; Baraquet et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The c-di-GMP reporter is activated in a subset of wild type PAO1 cells within 1 hr of surface attachment and remains activated in approximately 60% of PAO1 cells during the first 6 hr of attachment.
source: The c-di-GMP reporter is activated in a subset of wild type PAO1 cells within 1 hr of surface attachment and remains activated in approximately 60% of PAO1 cells during the first 6 hr of attachment.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In PA14, the c-di-GMP reporter is activated in a smaller proportion of attached cells compared to PAO1.
source: In PA14, the c-di-GMP reporter is activated in a smaller proportion of attached cells compared to PAO1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: By 1 hr after surface attachment, the reporter was activated in a subset of surface attached cells.
source: However, by 1 hr, the reporter was activated in a subset of surface attached cells, as defined by background subtracted GFP fluorescence ≥321 fluorescence units (referred to as reporter 'on' subpopulations).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from flow cell microscopy.

claim: Between 4 and 6 hr post inoculation, the c-di-GMP reporter was only active in a subset of cells in both PAO1 and PA14 strains.
source: Interestingly, between 4 and 6 hr post inoculation, we consistently observed that the c-di-GMP reporter was only active in a subset of cells in both strains (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: In PA14, the reporter was activated in 10% of the population over 6 hr, whereas PAO1 displayed greater reporter activity, with 40–60% of the cells displaying reporter activity through 12 hr.
source: In PA14, the reporter was activated in 10% of the population over 6 hr, whereas PAO1 displayed greater reporter activity, with 40–60% of the cells displaying reporter activity through 12 hr (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The reporter 'on' subpopulation represents cells with a range of high c-di-GMP levels.
source: We plotted each cell's individual fluorescence values over time and observed populations of cells with low and high c-di-GMP reporter activity at each timepoint after the 0 hr (Figure 1—figure supplement 3). We also observed long tails of high GFP fluorescence, particularly at 2 and 4 hr. This suggests that the reporter 'on' subpopulation represents cells with a range of high c-di-GMP levels.
evidence: This is an inference based on the distribution of fluorescence values shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The median fluorescence intensity was significantly different at every time point except between 4 and 6 hr, and between 8, 10, and 12 hr.
source: We found that the median fluorescence intensity was significantly different at every time point except between 4 and 6 hr, and between 8, 10, and 12 hr (Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by bootstrap analysis of single cell fluorescence data.

claim: c-di-GMP signaling is initiated rapidly upon surface attachment in the first 4–6 hr for a subpopulation of attached cells, while the rate of c-di-GMP increase tends to level off at later timepoints.
source: Together, these single cell analyses support a model in which c-di-GMP signaling is initiated rapidly upon surface attachment in the first 4–6 hr for a subpopulation of attached cells, while the rate of c-di-GMP increase tends to level off at later timepoints.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data based on single cell analyses.

claim: pPsiaA::gfpASV reporter activity resembles that of pPcdrA::gfpASV in response to a surface.
source: We found that pPsiaA::gfpASV reporter activity resembled that of pPcdrA::gfpASV in response to a surface (Figure 1—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: There is an enrichment of TRITC-conjugated lectin staining in the population of cells with high c-di-GMP reporter activity.
source: After 4 hr of attachment to glass, we observed an enrichment of TRITC-conjugated lectin staining in the population of cells with high c-di-GMP reporter activity (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 7), demonstrating that the subpopulation of cells with high c-di-GMP is producing more exopolysaccharide than their low c-di-GMP counterparts.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 7.

claim: Both the pel and psl operon transcripts were elevated in the reporter 'on' subpopulation, relative to the reporter 'off' subpopulation.
source: Both the pel and psl operon transcripts were elevated in the reporter 'on' subpopulation, relative to the reporter 'off' subpopulation (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: With respect to c-di-GMP signaling, there are at least two distinct subpopulations that arise shortly after surface attachment.
source: These data support that, with respect to c-di-GMP signaling, there are at least two distinct subpopulations that arise shortly after surface attachment.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing differences in reporter activity and polysaccharide production.

claim: Strains with mutations in the Pil-Chp chemosensory system were not significantly defective in surface sensing activity.
source: Strains with mutations in the Pil-Chp chemosensory system were not significantly defective in surface sensing activity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing no significant difference in reporter activity for ΔsadC and ΔpilY1 mutants.

claim: Deletion of the diguanylate cyclase activated through the Pil-Chp system (PAO1 ΔsadC) and the gene encoding the putative sensor PilY1 (PAO1 ΔpilY1) did not significantly influence reporter activity in response to a surface.
source: Deletion of the diguanylate cyclase activated through the Pil-Chp system (PAO1 ΔsadC) and the gene encoding the putative sensor PilY1 (PAO1 ΔpilY1) did not significantly influence reporter activity in response to a surface (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: A mutant lacking the main Type IV pilus filament protein (PAO1 ΔpilA) showed a statistically significant defect in reporter activity by 6 hr.
source: Whereas both the SadC and PilY1 mutants displayed wild type levels of reporter activity, a mutant lacking the main Type IV pilus filament protein (PAO1 ΔpilA) did show a statistically significant defect in reporter activity by 6 hr (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B; p<0.05 by T-test).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The PAO1 ΔwspR strain exhibited extremely low levels of reporter activity during the first 6 hr after surface attachment.
source: We found that the PAO1 ΔwspR strain exhibited extremely low levels of reporter activity during the first 6 hr after surface attachment (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Complementation of PAO1 ΔwspR restored wild type levels of activity at all time points.
source: Complementation of PAO1 ΔwspR restored wild type levels of activity at all time points (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: PAO1 ΔwspF had a high proportion of reporter active cells.
source: As expected, PAO1 ΔwspF had a high proportion of reporter active cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: PA14 displays a similar trend for Wsp mutants as PAO1.
source: We repeated these experiments in the lab strain PA14 and saw a similar trend for Wsp mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: A deletion mutant of PA5017 still exhibited heterogeneity during surface sensing.
source: We ruled out the phosphodiesterase (PA5017) as responsible for the heterogeneity we see during surface sensing by examining a deletion mutant of PA5017 and showing that this strain still exhibited heterogeneity during surface sensing (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: Reporter activity was very low in polarly attached cells, while cells attached along the entire length of the cell body displayed a higher proportion of reporter-activated cells at that same time point.
source: We found that reporter activity was very low in polarly attached cells, while cells attached along the entire length of the cell body displayed a higher proportion of reporter-activated cells at that same time point (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The finding that laterally attached cells have higher c-di-GMP levels is consistent with the localization of the Wsp system and its role for early c-di-GMP signaling during surface sensing.
source: This finding is consistent with the localization of the Wsp system and its role for early c-di-GMP signaling during surface sensing.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and known localization of the Wsp system.

claim: After a short period of growth on an agar surface, WspR-YFP clusters were visible in 30–40% of wild type PAO1 cells, and this is dependent on sensing by the membrane-bound protein WspA.
source: However, after a short period of growth on an agar surface, WspR-YFP clusters were visible in 30–40% of wild type PAO1 cells, and this is dependent on sensing by the membrane-bound protein WspA, which is laterally distributed in cells (Kuchma et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: A WspR[E253A] point mutation abolishes diguanylate cyclase activity, but this protein still forms clusters in about 70% of surface-grown cells.
source: A WspR[E253A] point mutation abolishes diguanylate cyclase activity, but this protein still forms clusters in about 70% of surface-grown cells (Huangyutitham et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: In the presence of inducer, there was a large increase in c-di-GMP reporter activity in WspR[L170D], but not WspR[E253A].
source: As expected, in the presence of inducer, we observed a large increase in c-di-GMP reporter activity in WspR[L170D], but not WspR[E253A] (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: pPcdrA::mTFP1 activity was significantly higher in cells with at least one subcellular WspR-eYFP focus in the WspR[L170D] strain compared to cells without a WspR-eYFP focus.
source: We found that pPcdrA::mTFP1 activity was significantly higher in cells with at least one subcellular WspR-eYFP focus in the WspR[L170D] strain compared to cells without a WspR-eYFP focus (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The heterogeneity observed in c-di-GMP signaling after surface attachment is due to the heterogeneity in the activity of the Wsp system, as reflected by subcellular clustering of active WspR-P.
source: These data indicate that the heterogeneity observed in c-di-GMP signaling after surface attachment is due to the heterogeneity in the activity of the Wsp system, as reflected by subcellular clustering of active WspR-P.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data linking WspR clustering to reporter activity.

claim: A PAO1 ΔwspR mutant was defective for biofilm formation relative to wild type PAO1 at 2, 4, and 6 hr post-attachment.
source: We performed in vitro biofilm assays and observed that a PAO1 ΔwspR mutant was defective for biofilm formation relative to wild type PAO1 at 2, 4, and 6 hr post-attachment (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: At later stages of development (24 hr), the wspR mutant caught up and produced similar amounts of biofilm biomass relative to wild type.
source: However, at later stages of development (24 hr), the wspR mutant caught up and produced similar amounts of biofilm biomass relative to wild type .
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from biofilm assays.

claim: Complementation of the ΔwspR strain in trans restored wild type levels of biofilm formation at all time points.
source: Complementation of the ΔwspR strain in trans restored wild type levels of biofilm formation at all time points (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The Wsp system rapidly responds to surface contact to generate elevated levels of c-di-GMP in a subpopulation of cells, which accelerates biofilm production.
source: These data suggest that the Wsp system rapidly responds to surface contact to generate elevated levels of c-di-GMP in a subpopulation of cells, which accelerates biofilm production.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data showing early biofilm defects in the wspR mutant.

claim: One of the many other known c-di-GMP cyclases present in P. aeruginosa may ultimately compensate for c-di-GMP production in the absence of WspR.
source: Given the importance of c-di-GMP signaling in biofilm production, the fact that the ΔwspR strain can ultimately attain wild-type levels of biofilm biomass suggests that one of the many other known c-di-GMP cyclases present in P. aeruginosa may ultimately compensate for c-di-GMP production in the absence of WspR.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation that the wspR mutant eventually forms wild-type levels of biofilm.

claim: There are clear inverse correlations between Ic-di-GMP and Fmotile and between Ic-di-GMP and λ for entire lineages in family trees.
source: Interestingly, when analyzing correlations between c-di-GMP and motility for entire lineages in family trees, we found clear inverse correlations between Ic-di-GMP and Fmotile (Figure 4B, ρ = −0.53, p=0.0012) and between Ic-di-GMP and λ (Figure 4C, ρ = −0.45, p=0.0068), suggesting that c-di-GMP levels are strongly inversely correlated with surface motility behavior and detachment behavior over multiple generation of cells.
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracking data shown in Figure 4B and 4C.

claim: Families with the highest Ic-di-GMP had the lowest Fmotile and λ.
source: Families with the highest Ic-di-GMP had the lowest Fmotile and λ (Family 1, Figure 4B–E).
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracking data shown in Figure 4B–E.

claim: In families with highest Ic-di-GMP, daughter cells remained attached following cell division, exhibited continuously elevated c-di-GMP, did not move appreciable distances on the surface, and ultimately produced small microcolonies.
source: In these families, daughter cells remained attached following cell division, exhibited continuously elevated c-di-GMP, did not move appreciable distances on the surface, and ultimately produced small microcolonies.
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracking data and spatial trajectories.

claim: Families of cells with low Ic-di-GMP had the highest Fmotile and λ.
source: In contrast, families of cells with low Ic-di-GMP had the highest Fmotile and λ.
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracking data.

claim: For families with low Ic-di-GMP, daughter cells frequently detached or traveled outside the field of view, had lower c-di-GMP levels, traveled larger distances on the surface, and ultimately did not form microcolonies.
source: For these families, daughter cells frequently detached or traveled outside the field of view, had lower c-di-GMP levels, traveled larger distances on the surface, and ultimately did not form microcolonies (Family 3, Figure 4B–E).
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracking data shown in Figure 4B–E.

claim: The WspR mutant has overall lower surface motility and lacks correlations between c-di-GMP, surface motility, and detachment behavior.
source: What our analysis revealed about the ΔwspR strain was quite unexpected: The WspR mutant has overall lower surface motility and, importantly, lacks correlations between c-di-GMP, surface motility, and detachment behavior (both at the level of lineages and at the level of single cells).
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracking data for the ΔwspR mutant.

claim: 23% of ΔwspR mutant cells have non-zero Fmotile compared to 44% of WT cells.
source: For single cell surface motility, 23% of ΔwspR mutant cells (48 of 210 cells) have non-zero Fmotile (the metric for surface motility) compared to 44% of WT cells (251 of 565 cells; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by single cell tracking data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Wsp system is involved in translating the heterogeneous c-di-GMP signaling events into the corresponding motility-related responses for cells and their progeny.
source: The overall lowered surface motility and the lack of correlations between c-di-GMP and surface motility in the ΔwspR mutant suggest that the Wsp system is involved in translating the heterogeneous c-di-GMP signaling events into the corresponding motility-related responses for cells and their progeny.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data showing differences between WT and ΔwspR mutant.

claim: The Wsp system's multi-generational temporal propagation of surface sensing signaling and behavior is important for the generation of heterogeneous populations of surface motile and immotile cells during early biofilm formation.
source: Therefore, the Wsp system's multi-generational temporal propagation of surface sensing signaling and behavior is important for the generation of heterogeneous populations of surface motile and immotile cells during early biofilm formation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing the role of WspR in correlating c-di-GMP with motility.

claim: Families that were not stimulated with light demonstrated a heterogeneous surface response similar to that of Families 1–3 in Figure 4B–E.
source: Families that were not stimulated with light demonstrated a heterogeneous surface response (Video 1 and Figure 5B,D) similar to that of Families 1–3 in Figure 4B–E.
evidence: This is supported by optogenetic experiment data shown in Figure 5B,D and Video 1.

claim: In families stimulated with light for more than one generation, the resulting c-di-GMP production artificially forced lineages to have low surface motility and commit to microcolony production.
source: In contrast, in families stimulated with light for more than one generation, the resulting c-di-GMP production artificially forced lineages to have low surface motility and commit to microcolony production (Video 1 and Figure 5A,C) similar to that of Family one in Figure 4B–E.
evidence: This is supported by optogenetic experiment data shown in Figure 5A,C and Video 1.

claim: Families stimulated with light had higher Ic-di-GMP and lower λ values than those that were not stimulated.
source: Families stimulated with light in this manner had higher Ic-di-GMP and lower λ values than those that were not stimulated (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by optogenetic experiment data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Optogenetic control of c-di-GMP results in phenotypes that are consistent with the wild-type behavior, with illuminated cells (high c-di-GMP) displaying the least motility and control (non-illuminated) cells displaying comparatively greater surface motility.
source: We also found that optogenetic control of c-di-GMP results in phenotypes that are consistent with the wild-type behavior presented in Figure 4, with illuminated cells (high c-di-GMP) displaying the least motility and control (non-illuminated) cells displaying comparatively greater surface motility (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by optogenetic experiment data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Families stimulated with light for one generation or less are not significantly different from un-illuminated controls.
source: Interestingly, families stimulated with light for one generation or less are not significantly different from un-illuminated controls (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the optogenetic experiments.

claim: The generation of c-di-GMP can deterministically lead to the creation of an entire lineage of sessile cells with post-division surface persistence, low motility, and initiation of microcolony formation.
